```text
# PR #1683: Patch: the AI sees an opponent's lethal that takes more than one attack

Closes #1634

## Summary

The AI imagines the opponent's next turn before it moves. In that imagined turn, the opponent now sees a lethal that needs more than one attack, but only when a new switch is on, and the switch ships **off** because the 400-game screen did not keep it (#1628's terms).

**Screen: 400 games on improve-dev, 203-197, edge 0.015 (−0.002 to 0.032) vs control 82d7eb4b8: not kept. Shipped value: `AI_REPLY.open_lethal = false`.**

With the switch off the AI plays exactly as it does on `main`: the new check is skipped entirely and attacks are ranked as before.

## What changed

- **`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`**
  - When the switch is on, each step of the opponent's imagined turn asks once whether the attacks it has left would together reach the AI's hero past its Taunts (the existing `lethal::ready_gap(&current, opp) <= 0.0` check). If so, every attack on that hero counts as the win, so the face goes first instead of a kill.
  - `ranked_attacks` takes that answer as a parameter.
  - The Deft switch trial still ranks one hit at a time.
  - New `pub fn simulate_reply_with(…, open_lethal)`; `simulate_reply` keeps its signature and passes `AI_REPLY.open_lethal`. The file header's step 3 describes the new rule.
- **`crates/ai/src/config.rs`**: new `AiReply.open_lethal: bool`, set to `false` with the screen's numbers in the comment beside it.
- **`crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`**: new `mod open_lethal_1634` with two tests:
  - `b41_takes_a_lethal_that_needs_both_attacks_over_a_kill_worth_more_than_one_hit`: two `core-025` against Mr. Vanilla `core-008` at 8 health. With the switch on, the opponent wins with two face hits in 2 nodes. With it off, today's behaviour holds: Mr. Vanilla dies and the AI lives on 1. `simulate_reply` follows the shipped switch.
  - `decide_blocks_one_of_two_attackers_that_are_lethal_only_together`: a full AI turn followed by the opponent attacking with everything. The AI survives exactly when the switch is on. I ran it both ways: on, it survives; off, it dies, as it does today.
- **SPEC §9.9** and **`docs/polish/3-ai.md`** ("Trades"): one sentence on the rule, each saying it is switched off until a screen keeps it.
- No ruling: this is how the AI plays, not a game rule, as with #1612 and #1628.

## Testing

All commands were run in this worktree:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai reply::`: 31 passed with the switch on and again with it off. The existing B41 tests are unchanged.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, switch on: lib 9, `ai` 520, `ai_slow` 79 passed (4 ignored, the existing daily tests).
- With the final `false`: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai` passed 9 and 520; `--test ai_slow` passed 79 (4 ignored).
- `cargo jackioh gate`, final `false`: 20, 14 and 17 of 20 against 17, 10 and 16 needed, the same as the base.
- `cargo jackioh gate`, switch on: 20, 14 and 16 of 20. It passes, but hard-vs-easy has no game to spare.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `patches check`, `spec check` (1092 rulings): ok.
- `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`: `Internal`, exit 0.
- Screen: the control was built before any edit and the candidate with the switch on. I ran `/tmp/jackioh-candidate-1634 arena --a self --b bin:/tmp/jackioh-control-1634 --set improve-dev --out /tmp/screen-1634` once, not re-run or extended. Its closing tally was `{"games":400,"aWins":203,"bWins":197,"draws":0,"aborted":0,"edge":0.015,"edgeLow":-0.002,"edgeHigh":0.032}`.
- Not run: the full `cargo test --workspace`, which the harness runs next. With the switch off, no code outside `jackioh-ai` behaves any differently.
- Not run: the web tests (plan step 12). They are required only if `true` ships.

## Where I departed from the plan

- **Control commit.** The plan named base `653d59cd1`, but the branch's base is now `82d7eb4b8`. The control was built from `82d7eb4b8`, and the config comment names it.
- **Name in `docs/polish/3-ai.md`.** I wrote `AI_REPLY.openLethal` rather than `open_lethal`, because that doc uses the camelCase names throughout (`AI_REPLY.knownPlays`, `readyGap`). The spec, which uses Rust names (`AI_SEARCH.max_auto_answer_options`), says `open_lethal`.
- **One extra clause in that doc.** The Deft trial's sentence there now says "ranked one hit at a time", to match the code and the header.
- The rest follows the plan's decisions: the switch is a field of `AI_REPLY` rather than a separate constant, and `ranked_attacks` takes the lethal answer from its caller so each step reads the board once.

## Worth a second look

- **The decision test follows the shipped switch.** `decide` cannot take the switch as an argument, so with it off the test pins today's behaviour, where the AI dies. Turning the switch on later makes the same test require the block, and I confirmed it passes that way.
- **Strength.** This screen does not show the rule makes the AI stronger, and with the switch on the smoke gate's hard-vs-easy run passed with no game to spare (16 of 16 needed). Turning the switch on should wait for a screen that keeps it.
```

**Issue #1634 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1634: Patch: the AI sees an opponent's lethal that takes more than one attack
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Before it moves, the practice AI imagines the opponent's next turn to see what its move leaves it open to. In that imagined turn the opponent only notices a win when one attack is enough. When two attackers would finish the AI only together, the imagined opponent often spends one of them killing a unit instead. The AI then thinks it survives, plays greedily, and loses to the two obvious swings. Once this is built, the AI sees those boards coming and spends its turn blocking, healing or removing an attacker. Players notice the AI stop walking into lethal they could see.

## Why
- The opponent's reply works as "a static trader": "of every attack it may declare, it takes the one with the best value read off the layers (lethal, a kill it survives, a trade up, the face)" (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:14-15`).
- `reply_face_value` (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:109-115`) returns `AI_EVAL.win` only when that one hit's `damage >= effective_life(state, seat)`. Otherwise it scores `AI_REPLY.face_per_damage` (1.0, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:676`) per point.
- A kill scores the target's whole `unit_worth` (`trade_value`, `reply.rs:92-103`). So the trader takes any kill worth more than an attacker's damage, even when the attacks together are lethal.
- `simulate_reply` (`reply.rs:358-433`) takes the top of `ranked_attacks` one attack at a time and never asks whether the attacks left can reach the face.
- The check the fix needs already exists. `lethal::ready_gap` (`crates/ai/src/lethal.rs:171-200`) sums what the units that may still attack would deal past the Taunts, and "zero or less means the attacks left could end the game".
- The only lethal test for the reply, `b41_takes_lethal_when_the_face_is_in_reach` (`crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs:81`), has a single attacker.

## Proposal
In the static-trader step of `simulate_reply`, ask `ready_gap(&current, opp) <= 0.0`. When it is, rank attacks on the seat's hero as the win, so the face goes first while the open attacks still reach it. Otherwise keep today's ranking. That is one board read per reply step, with no new search and no extra nodes.

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` (`ranked_attacks` / `simulate_reply`)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`, plus one decision test in `crates/ai/tests/ai/`
- SPEC §9.9 and `docs/polish/3-ai.md` ("The opponent's reply"): one sentence on the new rule

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reply test, failing today (the game is not over): the AI's seat is at 8 health with one unit. The opponent has two units whose attacks only together reach 8, and either of them can kill the AI's unit. The builder picks cards whose kill outranks the hit, for instance Mr. Vanilla `core-008` facing two `core-025`. `simulate_reply` ends with the opponent winning.
- [ ] The existing single-attacker B41 reply tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Decision test: in a position where removing or blocking one of the two attackers is the only way to survive, `decide` picks such a line, and it does not today.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.
- [ ] The change is screened on the dev set as `training/improve.md` says (400 games against the committed AI), and the pull request states the result. A change the screen does not keep ships switched off behind its constant, as #1628's terms did.

## Size and risks
About 10 lines of code and 2–3 tests. It is AI work, so hard by CLAUDE.md rule 11. It changes the score of every line after which the opponent has lethal on board, and SPEC §9.9 records that earlier search changes did not move the gate's greedy matchup past noise. The screen is therefore the judge of strength, and the visible misplay is the reason to build it. Nothing hidden is read: `ready_gap` counts the attacks `legal_actions` offers on the determinized board the reply already plays on.
````
